parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity or presentation and no documented bathroom, border or organised police targeting, with patchwork provincial/city protections and statutes punishing transphobic harassment, but recourse is local and uneven and the national commission lacks enforcement. The main visitor-facing exposure is custody: trans women are housed in male dormitories, with mandatory head-shaving and safety dependent on inmate hierarchies and survival 'weddings', only partially mitigated by one southern annex segregation practice. Documented killings described by the national commission as a pattern of transfemicide, plus service exclusions with little consequence and a dated 2020 Pride arrest, indicate societal hostility with thin remedy. No per-capita rate is established, and hostile local dress ordinances have no documented enforcement. This is unremedied institutional exposure without daily universal exclusion, placing it in elevated risk.
